title: Ops incident brief templates and field checklist
content:
PURPOSE
This is a working draft: a compact set of briefing templates, field-checklist items, and customer-facing snippets to use during live incidents. Goal: make on-call comms fast, consistent, and low-friction without being overly formal. Keep this doc lightweight; extract canonical templates into the status-page generator once stabilized.

NOTES TO SELF (TODOs)
- Confirm legal-approved phrasing for data-exposure incidents with privacy@redwood (ticket: PRIV-89).
- Add translated customer notices (JP/EU) after we verify localization pipeline.
- Consider adding a short automated timeline generator for long incidents (see INF-412).

QUICK ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES (one-line)
- Incident Lead (IL): owns the public status messages and overall cadence.
- Communications lead (Comm): crafts customer emails and external blog post if needed.
- Tech lead (TL): owns technical updates and escalation to infra teams.
- War-room scribe: keeps timeline and action log.

WAR-ROOM FIELD CHECKLIST (use in first 10 minutes)
- Join bridge, confirm attendees (IL, TL, Comm, SRE oncall).
- Short summary: who noticed it, first observed time, severity guess.
- Affected surface: API / Hosted / Dedicated / Console / Private.
- Immediate mitigation attempts and results (commands, rollbacks, roll-forward).
- Customer impact level (no impact / degraded / partial outage / full outage).
- Decide cadence for status updates (every 15 / 30 / 60 mins).
- Assign action owners for each mitigation step.
- Scribe: start timeline (timestamped bullets).

TEMPLATE: STATUS PAGE SHORT (for first public post)
- Title: "Service degraded: text generation latency increased"
- Body (short): "We are investigating increased latency for text-generation requests. Some requests may see timeouts or slower response times. We will post updates here every 30 minutes and on our status page. Our engineering team is actively investigating."
- Impact: "Latency increase affecting <hosted-api / dedicated>"
- What we're doing: "Investigating root cause; restarting affected serving pools and collecting traces."
- Suggested customer action: "No immediate action required; retry after a few seconds or fallback to cached responses."
- Severity label: "Degraded — Partial"

TEMPLATE: STATUS PAGE DETAILED (follow-up update)
- Headline: "Partial outage resolved for model-serving region us-west1 — follow-up"
- Summary: "At 2024-10-05T14:12Z we detected elevated error rates from the serving runtime in us-west1. We identified a memory leak in a kernel path causing repeated container restarts. We mitigated by reverting the kernel selector to the last-known-good build and scaling up hot spares; error rate began to normalize at 2024-10-05T16:03Z."
- Timeline: list timestamps and brief actions (keep scribe updated).
- Customers affected: "Hosted API customers in us-west1; Dedicated clusters pinned to v2.1 may have experienced errors."
- Root cause (initial): "investigation in progress / suspected kernel selector regression"
- Next steps: "Postmortem and full root-cause analysis; targeted rollout of fix; follow-up in 72 hours with RCA."

CUSTOMER EMAIL: SHORT ALERT (for large-impact incidents)
Subject: "[Redwood] Incident affecting text generation in us-west1 — ongoing"
Body:
Hi —
We’re aware of an ongoing incident impacting text generation for some Redwood customers in us-west1. Our engineers are actively investigating; root cause suspected to be a runtime regression. We’ll provide updates on the status page (status.redwood.ai) and next update by 15:45 UTC. We apologize for the disruption.

If you are experiencing a critical production impact, reply to this message with your account id and contact preference and we will escalate.
Thanks,
Priya (SRE Incident Lead)

CUSTOMER EMAIL: RESOLUTION (after incident closed)
Subject: "[Redwood] Incident resolved — summary and next steps"
Body:
Hi —
The service disruption impacting text generation in us-west1 has been resolved as of 2024-10-05T16:03Z. Engineers reverted the runtime selector to the prior stable build and scaled remediation resources. We will publish a full postmortem on Confluence within 72 hours and notify impacted customers directly with any follow-up actions.
If you saw errors or missing outputs during the incident window and need assistance re-running jobs, reply with your request and we’ll prioritize support.
Thanks for your patience —
Priya (SRE Incident Lead)

INTERNAL SLACK SCRIPTS (channel: #sre-incident-bridge)
- Quick notify (first post): ":[ALERT] Investigating elevated latency/errors for hosted API (us-west1). Bridge: <link>. IL=Priya, TL=Ethan. Updates every 30m."
- Update template: ":hourglass_flowing_sand: Update — 15:30 UTC — Errors 18% -> 12%; retry recommended; IL=Priya; next at 16:00 UTC."
- Resolution: ":white_check_mark: Resolved — error rate down to baseline. Root cause: kernel-selector regression. Postmortem planned."

SOCIAL/EXTERNAL NOTES (when required)
- Keep tweets factual and minimal. No technical details beyond what’s on status page. Suggested tweet: "We're resolving an issue affecting text-generation latency for some customers in US-West. We'll post updates at status.redwood.ai. Apologies for the disruption."
- Do not speculate on security/data without sign-off from Security and Legal.

ESCALATION QUICK LINKS (useful ids)
- Pager duty runbook: PD-ONCALL-SRE (link in Confluence)
- Infra oncall Slack: #infra-oncall
- Exec Slack paging: @onscall-execs

SAMPLE INTERNAL BRIEF (1-paragraph quick blurb)
At 14:12 UTC we saw a spike in 5xxs for the hosted text-gen endpoint in us-west1 with increased latencies; preliminary traces show repeated container restarts tied to an optimized kernel path. IL Priya, TL Ethan, Comm Marco. Current mitigation: reverted kernel selector and scaled extra replicas; error rate improving. Next update 15:00 UTC.

DECISIONING GUIDELINES (how to choose wording)
- If impact is "partial outage" and <10% customers affected: use "degraded" language and avoid escalation to execs unless SLAs are breached.
- If impact includes data loss/exposure: stop public posts until legal signs off; send internal notification to security@redwood immediately.
- If Dedicated customers affected due to tenant isolation failure: notify CSMs with targeted email template (CSM copied).

POST-INCIDENT HANDOFF (immediately after incident)
- IL writes short incident summary (3 bullets) and posts to #sre-postmortems draft channel.
- Create INF ticket (if not already) and attach timeline + key logs.
- Schedule RCA owner and target date (72 hours for initial RCA outline).

MINIMUM TIMELINE LOG FORMAT (scribe)
- 2024-10-05T14:12Z — Alert: elevated 5xx rate detected by synthetic tests.
- 2024-10-05T14:20Z — Bridge created; IL priya@redwood; TL ethan@redwood.
- 2024-10-05T14:35Z — Mitigation: rolled back kernel selector on pool-a. Error rate decreased from 22% -> 15%.
- 2024-10-05T15:03Z — Scaled hot spares; errors 8%.
- 2024-10-05T16:03Z — Baseline restored; bridge closed.

EXAMPLE CUSTOMER-FACING FAQ (short answers)
Q: Was customer data exposed?
A: We have no evidence of customer data exposure. The incident related to runtime kernel behavior causing service restarts. Security is reviewing logs as a precaution.

Q: Do I need to take action?
A: No. If you saw errors during the window and need re-runs or checks, contact support and include the account id and timestamp.

ARCHIVAL & FOLLOW-UP (after closure)
- Save final status page history to Confluence link in INF ticket.
- Comm lead drafts customer-facing RCA and coordinates with sales/CS for dedicated customers.
- Update status page canned messages library if wording proved confusing.

SKELETON POSTMORTEM ACTIONS (starter list)
- Reproduce locally: TL to provide reproduction steps.
- Fix permanent: patch kernel selector logic + add unit/regression tests.
- Improve detection: add a new synthetic that exercises this kernel path.
- Documentation: add operator notes in runbook for quick rollback.

OPEN QUESTIONS (to resolve in RCA)
- Why did the runtime kernel selector pick the bad path only in us-west1?
- Were any dedicated clusters pinned after the fix and did they remain affected?
- Telemetry gaps: need more granular traces for KV cache behavior.

END NOTES / REMINDERS
- Keep external posts concise and not technical unless customers request detail.
- When in doubt, escalate to Comm + Legal before posting about security/data.
- This doc is living. Add proven-good phrasing back into the status generator templates repo.

(rough draft, feel free to chop into smaller templates; aim to sync with comms playbook next week)
